spectral.true_color: Water is very dark blue-green to nearly black; land is muted green, olive and gray, with brighter gray-beige margins and scattered interior patches (high confidence). The strongest contrast follows shorelines, while vegetation interiors show subtler mottling (high confidence).
spectral.false_color: Most substantial land patches appear moderately to strongly red, with spatial variation in saturation and brightness (high confidence). Water remains dark navy-black, and many land margins become pale cyan-gray (high confidence). Small islands contain both red centers and pale edges (high confidence).

implications.claim: Vegetation occupies most island interiors; its red false-color response is consistent with substantial near-infrared scattering by foliage.
Variation in red intensity may reflect vegetation cover, canopy structure, species, substrate exposure or illumination; it does not independently establish differences in vegetation health.
Dark water is consistent with low near-infrared reflectance. No conspicuous bright sediment plume is visible.
The water may have relatively little visible suspended sediment, but depth, dissolved organic matter and display scaling prevent a reliable turbidity estimate.
Pale margins probably include exposed mineral substrate or sparse vegetation, although shallow water and mixed pixels may contribute.
The images do not establish vegetation moisture status, soil wetness or drought stress.
There are no clearly resolved built surfaces; isolated pale patches cannot reliably be classified as buildings, roads or bare soil.

spectral.not_revealed: These display renderings do not provide calibrated reflectance, reliable vegetation indices, water depth, salinity, quantitative turbidity, species identity, canopy height, soil moisture or change through time (high confidence). Their stretches may differ, so brightness cannot be compared quantitatively between renderings (high confidence).

interpretation.evidence: Levels 1, 2 and 4, northern and eastern land cells: mottled vegetated islands with pale margins. These traits are not geographically or climatically unique.

uncertainties: Cover percentages are visual estimates rather than measured segmentation; uncertainty is several percentage points, especially for pale margins and sparse vegetation (medium confidence).
At 10 m, small buildings, narrow paths, individual trees and tiny channels may be unresolved or mixed within pixels (high confidence).
Upsampling smooths boundaries without adding spatial information; exact island counts and narrow land connections remain uncertain (high confidence).
Feature dimensions are approximate measurements from the stated patch extent, with greater relative uncertainty for objects only a few pixels across (high confidence).
Pale shoreline pixels may represent rock, sediment, sparse vegetation, shallow bottoms or land-water mixing (medium confidence).
The compact dark inland patch may be a small water body, canopy shadow or another low-reflectance surface (low confidence in any specific identification).
Forest, shrubland and other dense vegetation cannot be separated reliably from these renderings alone (high confidence).
Water depth, clarity, salinity and whether the system is coastal or inland remain unresolved (high confidence).
No obvious cloud obscuration is visible, but small dark patches cannot be assigned confidently to cloud or terrain shadows (medium confidence).
Season, climate, management history and active change cannot be established from this single paired observation (high confidence).

summaries.w25: Vegetated islands and irregular shores surround connected dark water (high confidence). Water covers approximately 61% (medium confidence); season and coastal versus inland setting remain unresolved.
summaries.w50: Connected dark water surrounds irregular vegetated islands (high confidence), occupying approximately 61% of the patch (medium confidence). Red false-color interiors indicate vegetation (high confidence); pale shorelines suggest exposed substrate or mixed pixels (medium confidence). Coastal versus inland setting, season, vegetation health and management remain unresolved (high confidence).
summaries.w100: The patch shows connected dark water surrounding irregular vegetated islands and edge landmasses (high confidence). Estimated cover is 61% water, 31% vegetation and 8% pale substrate or shoreline mixtures (medium confidence). Larger landmasses occupy the north and southeast; broad water dominates the southern center (high confidence). Red false-color interiors indicate vegetation, while pale margins may include exposed rock, sparse cover or shallow-water mixtures (medium confidence). No clear fields, roads or settlement patterns are resolved (high confidence). Season, water properties, vegetation health and coastal versus inland setting remain uncertain (high confidence).
summaries.w200:
An island-rich water landscape dominates this 1.2 km patch (high confidence). Visual estimates assign 61% to water, 31% to vegetation and 8% to pale substrate, sparse cover and shoreline mixtures (medium confidence). The largest northern landmass extends southward between channels; smaller western islands and southeastern edge land surround a broad central-southern water area (high confidence).

Land is mottled green-gray in true color and broadly red in false color, supporting substantial vegetation cover (high confidence). Woody vegetation is plausible, but forest and shrub cover cannot be separated reliably (medium confidence). Pale irregular margins suggest exposed substrate, potentially rock, with shallow water and pixel mixing also contributing (medium confidence).

Water remains dark in both renderings, with no conspicuous sediment plume (high confidence); this does not establish depth, clarity or salinity. No clear agricultural parcels, road network, settlement or harvest blocks are resolved (high confidence). The scene appears predominantly natural or weakly modified (medium confidence). Season, ecological health, management and active shoreline change remain unresolved (high confidence). A temperate or boreal setting is plausible but weakly constrained (low confidence).
summaries.w400:
The two renderings show an island-rich landscape with connected dark water, irregular vegetated land and pale shoreline margins (high confidence). Approximate cover is 61% water, 31% vegetation and 8% exposed substrate, sparse vegetation or shoreline mixtures (medium confidence). These are visual estimates, with uncertainty concentrated along narrow margins and small islands.

The largest northern landmass extends approximately 550–600 m into the patch, tapering southward (medium confidence in size). A fragmented western island complex is separated from it by narrow channels. An elongated central island trends northwest-southeast, a compact island occupies the middle-right area, and a larger southeastern landmass enters from the eastern boundary (high confidence in layout). The southwest contains an edge landmass and a separate east-west elongated island. Broad connected water dominates bottom_center (high confidence). Numerous small detached patches are likely islets or rocks, although their exact count is uncertain (medium confidence).

Vegetated interiors are muted green-gray in true color and moderately to strongly red in false color (high confidence). Their near-infrared response supports foliage presence but does not establish physiological health, moisture status or species (high confidence). Mottled texture suggests woody vegetation on larger landmasses (medium confidence). Pale cyan-gray margins may combine exposed rock or sediment, sparse vegetation, shallow bottoms and mixed pixels (medium confidence).

Water is consistently dark, without a conspicuous bright sediment plume (high confidence). Turbidity, depth, salinity and whether the water is inland or coastal cannot be determined reliably (high confidence). No clear field boundaries, roads, settlement network or forestry cuts are resolved (high confidence); a predominantly natural or weakly modified landscape is therefore plausible (medium confidence).

There is no diagnostic evidence for active irrigation, harvest, clearing, erosion or flooding (high confidence in this observational limitation). A temperate or boreal wooded lake or archipelago is plausible, but biome and climate attribution have low confidence. Season is likewise weakly constrained because evergreen foliage could produce red land signatures outside summer. Upsampling does not resolve features smaller than the original 10 m pixels, limiting identification of buildings, paths, tiny channels and individual trees (high confidence).
